summary: Phase 23 triage batch review (plan 23-16, D-11). Every one of the 61 frozen triage population entries had an outcome (52 confirmed, 8 fixed by the Phase 22 rails, 1 unreproduced, 0 NOT-A-BUG), from three identical real-path runs (93 knownBug tuples from 56 files, 113 tests each) and one rail run (the 8 fixed entries' rail tests passed), recorded in inputs/triage-evidence.json and reported in plain language in 23-TRIAGE-REPORT.md. The operator was asked five numbered items: (1) acknowledge the 44 confirmed S0/S1 entries, each with its failing test (AC-18); (2) rule keep-open or not-a-bug on the one unreproduced entry, AUD-TX-006 (S3; AC-08); (3) whether the ESC-BUY-01 interim rule for AUD-BUY-001 (start the main bot right after any deliberate buy) should change now that AUD-ANTIRUG-025 shows a boot that resumes an open position drops its anti-rug watch; (4) a setup fact for AUD-ANTIRUG-018 (does any enabled chain run without a WebSocket address), not a ruling; (5) whether the four fork questions (AUD-ANTIRUG-003, AUD-BUY-015, AUD-BUY-033, AUD-EXIT-003) go to the Phase 25 fork run (AC-16). The reply addresses each item by number and name; no ruling was inferred from a general acknowledgement. Item 1 is recorded in acknowledged, item 2 in rulings, item 3 in decisions, item 4 in setup_answers and item 5 in fork_routing. No finding's escalation_ref changed and no escalation file was edited. No severity changed. Nothing was fixed; the bot stays off for all of v7.0.

The proven part (the Flashbots statistics call is made inside the wallet nonce lock, claim stats-call-inside-lock) is a real delay on the wallet; the open part (whether the relay still answers flashbots_getBundleStatsV2 for the bot's signer) could not be settled by the one approved request (HTTP 403, -32601 "rpc method is not whitelisted", inconclusive by the pre-fixed rule). The entry stays on the list (outcome unreproduced, status candidate, open claim endpoint-still-answers) and Phase 29 (card TX-03) removes or moves the call either way. No further Flashbots request is sent.

decisions.subject: Interim rule for AUD-BUY-001 (S0), weakened by AUD-ANTIRUG-025 (S1)
decisions.question: Item 3 of the report: the ESC-BUY-01 interim rule (Phase 22, carried on card BUY-01, numbered OD-26: after any landed deliberate buy start or restart the main bot at once) brings back the exit monitor but not anti-rug, because AUD-ANTIRUG-025 drops the anti-rug watch on every boot that resumes an open position. Options: (1) change the rule to "no deliberate buy until Phase 24 has fixed AUD-BUY-001 and AUD-ANTIRUG-025"; (2) keep the rule, read as covering the exit monitor only; (3) another rule the operator names.

decisions.supersedes: The ESC-BUY-01 interim rule "start the main bot right after any manual buy", recorded in escalations/ESC-BUY-01.json ruling_note and in decisions/OD-26.json interim_rule.

setup_answers.question: Item 4 of the report (a setup fact, not a ruling; the grade does not depend on it): does any enabled chain run without a WebSocket address? The report gave a one-line command that prints, for each entry of ENABLED_CHAINS (default eth), the chain, its <CHAIN>_WS_URL key and only "set" or "NOT set", never the address.
setup_answers.operator_words: 4. ANTIRUG-018: that command you sent me only output "eth ETH_WS_URL set"
setup_answers.fact: ENABLED_CHAINS is eth only (or unset, which defaults to eth) and ETH_WS_URL has a non-empty value. The executor did not read .env; the operator ran the check.
setup_answers.exposure_from_code: On this setup the bot never starts the HTTP anti-rug poller that AUD-ANTIRUG-018 is about. chainRegistry.ts:644 parses ENABLED_CHAINS with the same default (eth) and trimming; chainRegistry.ts:662 sets wsRpcUrl to process.env.ETH_WS_URL || null, the same truthiness the command printed; createChainContext (chainRegistry.ts:1066) calls getWsProvider, which returns null only for an empty URL (provider.ts:33-40) and otherwise a WebSocketProvider. startChainAntiRugListener takes the HTTP branch (startHttpPollingAntiRug, detector.ts:1224) only when ctx.wsProvider is falsy (detector.ts:590-603). Every later reassignment of ctx.wsProvider stores a newly built WebSocketProvider, never null: the anti-rug reconnect (detector.ts:923-929), the two DEX reconnect loops (bot.ts:1563-1564, bot.ts:1605-1606) and the dashboard Start callback (bot.ts:1814-1818, which takes the getWsProvider branch because the URL is set). There is no path that falls back to HTTP polling after a WebSocket failure or refused reconnect. So AUD-ANTIRUG-018 is not reachable on the operator's current setup; it becomes reachable as soon as any chain without a WebSocket address is enabled. The same holds for its DEX-listener sibling AUD-BUY-036 (bot.ts:1530-1533 picks HTTP polling only when ctx.wsProvider is null). The WebSocket path has its own confirmed outage findings that do apply on this setup: AUD-ANTIRUG-005 (backfill does not replay a real outage after a long healthy session) and AUD-ANTIRUG-002 (a refused WebSocket reconnect kills the process). The grade of AUD-ANTIRUG-018 (S1, ESC-ANTIRUG-03) does not change.
